title: 1  Relations
text:
A relation simply relates elements in two different sets by delineating a subset of related pairs in the Cartesian product.

Definition 1.1 (Relation) Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be sets. A relation over \(X \times Y\) is a subset \(R \subseteq X \times Y\).
If \(Y=X\), the relation is called homogeneous. When \((x,y)\in R\), we say that \(x\) is related to \(y\) and write \(xRy\).

The definition in Definition 1.1 treats a relation as a set of ordered pairs. Equivalently, its indicator is a proposition-valued function of two arguments.

Example 1.1 (Basic relations) Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be sets. The following are standard examples:

The discrete relation \(X\times Y\).
The empty relation \(\emptyset\subseteq X\times Y\).
When \(Y=X\), the diagonal relation \(\{(x,x):x\in X\}\).



Exercise 1.1 (Equality of the basic relations) Give a necessary and sufficient condition for the empty, discrete, and diagonal relations to be equal.






TipSolution





Assume the three are homogeneous relations on the same set \(X\), so \(Y=X\). They are equal if and only if \(X=\emptyset\).
If \(X=\emptyset\), then
\[
X\times X=\emptyset
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\{(x,x):x\in X\}=\emptyset,
\]
so all three relations coincide. Conversely, if the diagonal relation is empty, then \(X\) has no elements: any \(x\in X\) would make \((x,x)\) an element of the diagonal. Therefore \(X=\emptyset\).





Exercise 1.2 (Product of relations) Let \((X_1,R_1)\) and \((X_2,R_2)\) be pairs of sets and relations on them. The rule
\[
(x,y)\,(R_1\times R_2)\,(x',y')
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
xR_1x'\text{ and }yR_2y'
\]
defines a relation \(R_1\times R_2\) on \(X_1\times X_2\). Express this relation as a subset of \((X_1\times X_2)^2\).






TipSolution





The relation is
\[
R_1\times R_2
=
\left\{
\bigl((x,y),(x',y')\bigr)\in(X_1\times X_2)^2
:
(x,x')\in R_1\text{ and }(y,y')\in R_2
\right\}.
\]





Definition 1.2 (Equivalence relation) Let \(X\) be a set and \(R\) a relation over \(X\) as in Definition 1.1. We say \(R\) is

Reflexive if \(xRx\) for every \(x\in X\).
Symmetric if \(xRy\) implies \(yRx\) for all \(x,y\in X\).
Transitive if \(xRy\) and \(yRz\) imply \(xRz\) for all \(x,y,z\in X\).
An equivalence relation on \(X\) if it is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.


Notation. An arbitrary equivalence relation is typically denoted \(\sim\).
